stack.title: Saint Peter, the first pope
stack.hook: Saint Peter was the first pope according to Catholic tradition and one of Jesus's 12 apostles. But before any of that, he was a fisherman named Simon.

cards.head: Saint Peter was the first pope according to Catholic tradition and one of Jesus's 12 apostles.
cards.body: But before any of that, he was a fisherman named Simon.

cr.line: Caravaggio, Crucifixion of Saint Peter.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: JESUS CHANGED HIS NAME
cards.body: Jesus gives Simon the name Peter, derived from the Greek word for “rock.” The new name was the job: Peter is being made the foundation the church is built on.

cr.artwork: De verloochening van Petrus Rijksmuseum SK-A-3137.jpeg
cr.file: De verloochening van Petrus Rijksmuseum SK-A-3137.jpeg
cr.line: De verloochening van Petrus Rijksmuseum SK-A-3137.jpeg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: In Matthew, Jesus tells him, “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church,” a passage central to the Catholic understanding of the papacy.

cr.artwork: Saint Peter's Basilica Dome from Square Garden Vatican 14.jpg
cr.file: Saint Peter's Basilica Dome from Square Garden Vatican 14.jpg
cr.line: Saint Peter's Basilica Dome from Square Garden Vatican 14.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: HE WAS PART OF JESUS'S INNER CIRCLE
cards.body: Peter repeatedly appears as a leader among the apostles and witnesses major events including the Transfiguration. But the Gospels also portray him as impulsive, confused and occasionally spectacularly wrong.

cr.artwork: Raphael - The Transfiguration - Google Art Project.jpg
cr.file: Raphael - The Transfiguration - Google Art Project.jpg
cr.line: Raphael - The Transfiguration - Google Art Project.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: HE DENIED EVEN KNOWING JESUS
cards.body: After Jesus was arrested, Peter was asked three times whether he knew him. Three times Peter denied it, exactly as Jesus had predicted, before hearing a rooster crow.

cr.artwork: Civil war and rebellion in the Roman empire A.D. 69-70; companion to the "Histories" of Tacitus (1908) (14576214397).jpg
cr.file: Civil war and rebellion in the Roman empire A.D. 69-70; companion to the "Histories" of Tacitus (1908) (14576214397).jpg
cr.line: Civil war and rebellion in the Roman empire A.D. 69-70; companion to the "Histories" of Tacitus (1908) (14576214397).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: Jesus had told him it would happen before the bird crowed at dawn, so the crow is the moment Peter realises what he has done.

cr.line: Ancient Sea of Galilee Boat 1st Century AD at Yigal Allon Centre Ginosar Israel.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THEN HE BECAME A LEADER OF CHRISTIANITY
cards.body: After Jesus's death, Acts portrays Peter preaching publicly, performing healings and leading the earliest Christian community. Catholic tradition consequently regards him as the first pope.

cr.artwork: Giovanni Battista Castello - Christ Giving the Keys to St Peter - WGA04535.jpg
cr.file: Giovanni Battista Castello - Christ Giving the Keys to St Peter - WGA04535.jpg
cr.line: Giovanni Battista Castello - Christ Giving the Keys to St Peter - WGA04535.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: HE ENDED UP IN ROME
cards.body: Early Christian tradition holds that Peter eventually traveled to Rome and led its Christian community. During the reign of Nero, Roman emperor from 54 to 68 AD, he was reportedly sentenced to crucifixion.

cr.artwork: Joseph Martinez, grandfather of Pope Leo XIV.webp
cr.file: Joseph Martinez, grandfather of Pope Leo XIV.webp
cr.line: Joseph Martinez, grandfather of Pope Leo XIV.webp. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: TRADITION SAYS HE WAS CRUCIFIED UPSIDE DOWN
cards.body: A later Christian tradition says Peter asked to be crucified upside down because he didn't consider himself worthy to die exactly as Jesus had. St. Peter's Basilica now stands over the traditional location of his tomb.

cr.artwork: Christ between Sts Peter and Paul, Tomb of Emperor Otto II area - Vatican Grottoes.jpg
cr.file: Christ between Sts Peter and Paul, Tomb of Emperor Otto II area - Vatican Grottoes.jpg
cr.line: Christ between Sts Peter and Paul, Tomb of Emperor Otto II area - Vatican Grottoes.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THE LINE RUNS TO TODAY
cards.body: St. Peter's Basilica was built over the traditional site of his grave. Pope Leo XIV, elected in 2025, is counted as the 266th successor of that fisherman.

cr.line: Michelangelo Caravaggio 038.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: WHY A FISHERMAN STILL MATTERS
cards.body: The line from Peter to the current pope is the longest continuously claimed chain of office in the world. Every papal election restates that claim, so the story is never allowed to become historical.
